speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Could you tell me if you've noticed any yellowing of your skin or eyes, or changes in the color of your urine or stool?

speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old male. The patient reports a 2-month history of increasing generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. He has known hypertension and was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis 5 years ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and inconsistent condom use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of ulcerative colitis, have you noticed any darkening of your urine or light-colored stools, which would suggest bile duct obstruction? Also, do you have a history of gallstones or any family history of liver disease?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. I also have Scleral icterus, Multiple scratch marks on trunk and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of ulcerative colitis and current jaundice, I suspect an autoimmune liver condition, so I will request your latest liver function tests and an abdominal ultrasound. REQUEST TEST: Liver_Function_Panel REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_Ultrasound

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Liver Function Panel: Bilirubin_Total 1.5 mg/dL, Bilirubin_Direct 0.9 mg/dL, Alkaline_Phosphatase 460 U/L, AST 75 U/L, ALT 78 U/L, Anti-Nuclear_Antibody Negative, Antimitochondrial_Antibodies Negative. Abdominal Ultrasound: Thickening of the bile ducts and focal bile duct dilatation.

speaker: Doctor
text: The thickened bile ducts seen on your ultrasound, combined with your history of ulcerative colitis and negative autoimmune liver antibodies, strongly suggest Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis. To confirm this diagnosis, I need a more detailed visualization of your bile duct anatomy. REQUEST TEST: MRCP REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRCP: Beading appearance of intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts with multiple strictures and dilatations, consistent with Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis. No evidence of choledocholithiasis or malignancy.

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRCP confirms the beading and strictures consistent with Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis, which aligns perfectly with your history of ulcerative colitis. To assess the extent of liver fibrosis and rule out any associated complications like cholangiocarcinoma, I will request a liver biopsy and a tumor marker test. REQUEST TEST: Liver_Biopsy REQUEST TEST: CEA_and_CA19-9

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Liver Biopsy: Histology shows periportal fibrosis with onion-skin fibrosis around bile ducts, consistent with Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis. No evidence of hepatocellular carcinoma or cholangiocarcinoma. CEA and CA19-9: CEA 2.5 ng/mL (Normal), CA19-9 18 U/mL (Normal).

speaker: Doctor
text: The biopsy results showing onion-skin fibrosis, combined with your ulcerative colitis history and characteristic MRCP findings, confirm the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis
